title: test_multihop_latency_bounds.py: chaos tests still pass with zero deliveries; LatencyRule never waited out
description:
## Problem

`python/tests/sim/test_multihop_latency_bounds.py` chaos tests still skip their only bound checks when there are no samples:

- `test_latency_bounded_with_added_delay` (~L318-324): `if stats.count > 0 and stats.max_us is not None:` then assert max <= 350ms
- `test_latency_bounded_with_degraded_signal` (~L354-358): `if stats.count > 0 and stats.max_us is not None:` then assert max <= 300ms

If chaos drops every packet, both tests PASS without checking latency at all.

This is the same vacuous-pass class as closed `project-LICHEN-worker6-nvod` (concurrent) and `project-LICHEN-worker6-ffrp` (bursty). Those two tests were given real count asserts; these two were not.

## LatencyRule is never observed

`LatencyRule(node_id="relay", added_us=50_000)` sets `added_latency_us` on matching candidates. `radio.py` `_get_rx_result_internal` then drops candidates until:

    current_time_us >= transmission.end_time_us + added_latency_us

The test polls `get_rx_result("relay")` immediately after `start_transmission("src")` (in-flight, before end_time), so the delayed candidate is filtered out (`result` is None). It then `advance_to(+400_000)` without polling again, so the packet is never collected. Relay never forwards. `stats.count` is 0. The 50ms injection is not in the samples, and the `if stats.count > 0` guard hides that.

`python/examples/chaos_testing.py` notes that LatencyRule eligibility is `end_time_us + added_us`; this test does not wait for that.

Degrade -20dB at 80m may or may not deliver; if it does not, the same guard passes. If it does, recorded latency is still ~0 µs from the TX-start poll (see sibling finding on poll timing). Either path fails to show "degradation does not cause unbounded latency growth": there is no queue, and missed deliveries are treated as success.

## Not a duplicate of nvod/ffrp

nvod/ffrp fixed concurrent and bursty tests only. Chaos class remains unguarded.
design: Same vacuous-if pattern already removed from test_latency_under_concurrent_transmissions (nvod) and test_bursty_traffic_latency_bounded (ffrp). radio.py drops LatencyRule candidates until end_time_us + added_latency_us; BARRIER_SYNC in-flight poll happens before end_time, so the delay test currently records no deliveries.
acceptance_criteria: test_latency_bounded_with_added_delay and test_latency_bounded_with_degraded_signal assert stats.count >= MIN_DELIVERIES_FOR_STATS (fail, do not skip, when there are no samples). The LatencyRule test polls only after current_time_us >= tx_end + added_us so the 50ms delay is actually observed; max_us is asserted unconditionally and is at least the injected delay.
close_reason: Chaos tests require MIN_DELIVERIES_FOR_STATS. LatencyRule test polls only after current_time >= tx_end + added_us; radio.py keeps delayed candidates until then. Relay samples equal airtime+50ms; max asserted unconditionally.
